topic: Parallel and Perpendicular Lines and the Angle Between Them
title: Never Meet or Cross Square? Lines Explained Simply | Class 11 Maths
description:
On a town map some roads run side by side and never meet, and others cross perfectly square. How can you tell without drawing them forever? The secret is in their slopes. In this animated lesson for Class 11 Maths (NCERT Chapter 9, Straight Lines) we learn the slope tests for parallel and perpendicular lines and the formula for the angle between two lines.

You will watch one line turn live while its meeting point with another line runs away and disappears exactly when the slopes become equal, then keep turning until the crossing angle reaches 90 degrees and the slopes multiply to minus one. A quarter-turn picture shows why m1 times m2 is minus one, we build tan theta = |(m2 - m1) / (1 + m1 m2)| step by step, and find the sharp angle between lines with slopes 2 and -3. Two pause-and-think questions, the exam trap of only changing the sign, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Follows the NCERT book. Useful for CBSE, ICSE (ISC), Karnataka PUC and other state boards, and JEE.

In this video:
0:00 Roads that never meet, roads that cross square
0:22 Parallel lines: equal slopes
0:48 Live: turn a line, watch where they meet
1:19 Why perpendicular slopes multiply to -1
2:02 Parallel vs perpendicular
2:37 The angle between two lines
3:44 Worked example: slopes 2 and -3
4:18 Exam trap: flip and change the sign
4:45 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:23 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode (Ep 71): Point-Slope and Two-Point Forms of a Line. Two dots on a map: draw the road between them.
